outcome: Obstetric intervention for suspected fetal distress in labor
cohort: 562 low-risk term pregnancies, defined by the absence of maternal morbidity or pregnancy complication, accompanied by normal ultrasound and clinical screening of fetal growth in the third trimester, with spontaneous onset of labor
finding: While reduced CPR was associated with a higher risk of obstetric intervention due to fetal distress and composite adverse perinatal outcome, it was a poor predictor of adverse perinatal outcome in this cohort of low-risk term pregnancies.
